questions.question: When it is clear that you will turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes. This is true even if you think your intention is obvious. Other vehicles may be near you but out of sight.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights on during the day:

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than when their headlights are off.
They are less safe than when their headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than when their headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to help other drivers see you. This improves your visibility during the day and at night.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best grip for motorcycle tires. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, lane markings, and metal road covers are all more hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: One way to lower your crash risk is to:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of your lane that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your job to be seen.
Change to a different lane, if you can do so safely.
Weave within your lane to be more obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if possible. If another lane is not available, slow down to give the merging driver more space.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic without warning. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This creates more space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: When you slow down or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should also be able to reach and operate all controls easily.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) varies. It is safest to not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT need to be checked before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Look at the rims and spokes for bends, loose parts, or damage. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all your lights. The seat fabric does not affect safety.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the non-flat tire.
Increase your speed to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the non-flat tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep going straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because motorcyclists and other drivers may collide there more easily.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to increase your speed.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What happens when you take corners too fast?

options.text: You may go into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You usually stay in your lane.
It is fine because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn or take a curve.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
Avoid telling the passenger to wear protective gear.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that riders wear.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as these surfaces have less grip.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Less of your face than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How important are signals on a motorcycle?

options.text: More important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: More important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more at risk than car and truck drivers. This makes it even more important for motorcyclists to use signals.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: The same area as a face shield.
The same area as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes but not your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when stopping. Both brakes together stop your motorcycle most effectively.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
You stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, your wheels may lose grip and you could crash.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need to be checked before each ride?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, lights, electrical system, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint condition is not part of a pre-ride check.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel skidding and locking when you brake hard in straight lines. When sensors detect a wheel may lock, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep your brakes working at their best.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection to motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: How can you be more easily seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and ride in a position that lets you see oncoming traffic. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement for motorcyclists.

questions.question: A cushion of space while riding helps you to:

options.text: Have time to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, you should be able to see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. The road behind and to the side of you is most important.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, it means they:
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns or stops instead of mechanical turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to do a head check if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show the full view of the road around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can assume drivers will respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers day and night.

questions.question: In general, the body removes about ______ of alcohol per hour.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour on average.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: When riding on bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge grating may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually safe. Relax and continue at a steady speed. Trying to zigzag is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Can help you slow down using the engine.
Should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you slow down using the engine.
questions.explanation: Downshifting can help you slow down by using the engine. Use your brake lights when you do this so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is located on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To maintain control through a turn, look ahead by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear before riding. You do not need to check tire flexibility.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Make sure your motorcycle is set up and adjusted for a passenger.
Ride the same way you would without a passenger.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your motorcycle is set up and adjusted for a passenger.
questions.explanation: Carry a passenger only if your motorcycle has a passenger seat, separate footrests for the passenger, and proper adjustments for the extra weight. You may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume it handles the same as your own motorcycle.
Assume the owner checked the brakes for you.
Keep extra distance between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep extra distance between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.
questions.explanation: Do all safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle just as you would on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra space when stopping.
